subunit: Forms a tight complex with SCAP, the SCAP-SREBP complex, in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and the Golgi apparatus. Interacts with PAQR3; the interaction anchors the SCAP-SREBP complex to the Golgi apparatus in low cholesterol conditions. Interacts (via C-terminal domain) with RNF139

complexes.name: SREBP-SCAP transcription regulator complex, SREBF2 variant
complexes.function: When the cell is enriched with cholesterol. SCAP binds and stabilizes full-length SREBF1/2 and is anchored in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) by formation of the SREBP-SCAP-INSIG complex (CPX-25747/CPX-25748). Under conditions of low sterols, the SREBP-SCAP complex is translocated by COPII (CPX-2360)-coated vesicles from the ER to the Golgi where SREBF1/2 is proteolytically cleaved and freed from the membrane to activate the transcription of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis.
complexes.properties: SCAP consists of eight transmembrane helices connected by four small hydrophilic loops and three large loops. Two of the large loops (Loops 1 and 7) are in the ER lumen, and the other large loop (Loop 6) faces the cytosol where it binds COPII proteins to initiate transport of the complex to the Golgi. Cholesterol binding to Loop 1 alters the configuration of Loop 6, preventing COPII binding and the exit of SCAP from the ER.
